# dispositions"). Written by the BUILD side, never by the blinded author: l1d27_listing.tsv
# beside it is the author's and is not edited. check_listing.py reads both: every row the
# author recorded FAIL must name at least one limit here, and no PASS row may.
# LIMIT KEYS (one design sentence each; a key not declared here is a check error):
#   domain       F1. A consumed class outside the run's domain (more than
#                PCREC_MAX_REQ_RUN_POS_SET = 128 members: `.`, `[^z]`) is a gap, not a run
#                position (src/facts/req.c rb_class_into), so no guard meets it. span_arms
#                §5.1 "The guard" (positions are the sets the domain admits, D187 add. 1);
#                the unlock is §10 U-descguard (guards meet DESCRIPTION positions, where a gap
#   guard-domain F2. A guard is read term by term outward from the cursor and ends at the
#                first term outside the run's domain (span_arms §5.1 "The guard"), so a
#                lookbehind `(?<=x..)` keeps no term past its wide one; same unlock.
#   rep-wall     F3. The head's REP arm is a wall until [REPEAT-RUN] R2 (span_arms §14.3
#                D-10, "WHY THE REP WALL STAYS UNTIL R2"): a lookahead body with a counted
#                repeat yields no item past the repeat (`(?=(?:ab){2}c)`), counted by R2's
#   nested-item  F4. A nested positive lookaround is its OWN item (span_arms §5.1 ITEM,
#                ctx_span §3.6: items are conjoined, never merged) and reaches the run only
#                as the body's edge guards; its narrowing of the body's consumed positions
#                stays in the body (§14.3 D-1: the body's set, description and consumed runs
#                stay in the body), and the item reads the body's HEAD column (D-10), where a
#                lookaround is a unit read through. Unlock: span_arms §10 U-nesteditem.
#   edge-drop    F5. CAT-EDGE carries a leftover guard only across an `all` (exact-width)
#                neighbour and drops it otherwise (span_arms §14.3 D-3; §10 U-exactwidth is
#                the exact-width widening, for fixed-width neighbours only), and `dead` is one-sided (facts_listing §4.1.3¶1a
